articles.title: Divisions deepen between EU member states after tense budget summit
articles.summary: An EU leaders summit on the bloc's seven-year budget fell apart amid divisions over how to fund Ukraine. The budget proposal also includes a 3% tax on US tech companies, in a bid for the EU to…

image.caption: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz outlined his government's position to the press in Brussels after the November 2026 summit.Image: Marius Burgelman/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: EU leaders arrived in Brussels braced for a difficult showdown over the bloc's multitrillion-euro seven-year budget. But few expected the summit to unravel so quickly, with talks breaking down late on Thursday night.
Squabbles and thinly veiled public barbs meant they left without a deal and didn't even attempt to resume discussions on the planned second day.
There is a self-imposed deadline to find agreement before the end of 2026 on the budget which covers the 2028-2034 period. But experts say there is no cause for alarm, yet.

"Every time there are long-term EU budget negotiations, there are breakdowns, chaos, recrimination and a lot of political theater and drama," said Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, an EU economist and expert at the Bruegel think tank in Brussels.

The center of that political theater this time was the prime ministers of Denmark, Sweden, Belgium and Austria — countries wanting a reduced budget — who staged a walkout during smaller, group meetings, claiming the atmosphere had not been constructive to getting a deal.

Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar called the whole summit "completely unnecessary," pointing the blame at the man who had decided to call it and whose job it is to meditate the talks, European Council President Antonio Costa.
Costa was diplomatic in defending his decision to bring the leaders to Brussels, telling the press: "For me it was very useful to figure out the parameters of a possible landing zone in December."

blocks.caption: European Council President Antonio Costa was forced to defend his decision to call the summit which ended in acrimonyImage: Daniel Gnap/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: Germany demands more for competitiveness, security, defense

Long before the summit started, Germany had laid down an ultimatum — Berlin would only sign off on the budget if all the other EU countries greenlit an additional €45 billion ($49 billion) support loan for Ukraine to fund the country in its war efforts through 2027.

Hungary, Czechia, Bulgaria and Slovakia have dug their heels in against the proposal, insisting that giving Ukraine money to buy weapons will prolong the war. Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico even accused Germany of "blackmail."
Can Europe defend itself without the US?
As Europe's biggest economy, Germany's contribution amounts to around 25% of the whole budget.

In a press conference after the summit, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said "hundreds of billions" still need to be slashed. The European Commission's original proposal of approximately €1.786 trillion had already been reduced by €204 billion (down 10.2%).
"Europe needs to exercise a sense of proportion," said Merz. "The budget cannot grow indefinitely, and the burden of financing it must be distributed fairly."
Merz also aimed a comment toward Costa, who has been renewing the details in the budget proposal at every stage.
"The proposals that have been on the table so far are not a basis for an agreement," said Merz.
Costa did tell leaders on Thursday that he is planning to cut between €220 billion to €230 billion out of the next proposal.
Berlin's budget reduction push is backed by six other countries who together call themselves the "Sensible Seven." All pay more into the collective EU financial pot than they receive out of it.

blocks.caption: The leaders of the 'sensible seven' — Germany, Netherlands, Denmark, Belgium, Sweden, Finland and Austria — met separately at the Brussels summitImage: Frederic Sierakowski

blocks.text: They are opposed by 17 EU member states who insist the total budget should grow, led by France and Italy. These countries call themselves the "Friends of Cohesion" — a nod to the EU cohesion funds which are used to share wealth from the EU's richer regions and nations to its poorer ones.

In the current proposal, agriculture, fisheries and cohesion spending falls from 59.1% to 42.4%, while money for economic competitiveness, security, and defense rises from 17.7% to 27.7%. This rebalancing is a key German demand.
EU looking elsewhere to raise funds

The EU is also searching for a way to add money into the budget that doesn't come from national contributions. The current proposal includes a controversial EU-wide digital tax which could chart a course for a major battle with the US.

The idea, originally put forward by French President Emmanuel Macron, is for a 3% tax on revenues of online advertising, online marketplaces and on the monetization of user data. The money, to be paid directly into the EU's budget, is estimated to bring in €5 billion per year.
But the proposal is ringing alarm bells in Ireland where US tech giants like Google, Meta, Apple, Microsoft and LinkedIn are headquartered.
"A digital tax is sending out all the wrong messages," said Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin, who could still veto the proposal.
Protecting the EU's top triple-A rating
There is a fear in some European capitals that without being able to generate its own funds, future EU loans could downgrade the European Commission's unblemished standing on international markets.

The EU has around €860 billion in outstanding debts it took out for its pandemic recovery funding and to support Ukraine. Its triple-A credit rating could be downgraded if Marine le Pen, the far-right front-runner in France's presidential election, wins in the spring and follows through on her promise to reduce French contributions to the EU budget.

blocks.caption: If France's far-right challenger wins the spring 2027 election, it could change the whole shape of the EU budget negotiationsImage: Stephanie Lecocq/REUTERS

blocks.text: EU member states that favor a financing model through national contributions rather than through tax revenue "understand very well what will happen if the EU loses its triple-A rating," said Bruegel's Kirkegaard. "Interest rate costs will go up even more. Who has to pay for that? Net contributing countries, like Germany, the Nordics, the Dutch, which is why they are much more open to this than in the past."
Other European tax experts believe that prior examples of these digital taxes show the costs outweigh the benefits.

"We analyzed the states which have a digital services tax [DST], and we've seen that economic cost exceeds the revenue generated," said Cristina Enache, an economist at the Brussels-based nonprofit Tax Foundation Europe. "Spain has a DST and the expected revenue was twice or three times larger than what they actually are collecting."
Enache called the tax proposal "politically impossible."
EU leaders know that the clock on their end-of-2026 deadline is ticking, and will return to the same conference rooms in late December hoping for a more conducive atmosphere to strike a deal.

articles.title: Jared Kushner’s 70-minute interview shows the peril of treating Putin like a corporate rival
articles.summary:
Trump’s son-in-law and top negotiator paints Russian invasion of Ukraine as a misunderstanding to be resolved

In the space of a 70-minute interview, Jared Kushner – Donald Trump’s son-in-law…

blocks.text: In the space of a 70-minute interview, Jared Kushner – Donald Trump’s son-in-law and a prominent US negotiator in Russia, Gaza and Iran – probably did more to reveal why the world is mired in entrenched conflicts than a thousand geopolitical tomes or seminars.

During the conversation this week with Mathias Döpfner, the chief executive of the Axel Springer media publisher, Kushner gave a rare insight into his diplomatic technique, offering a string of homilies that veered close to banalities: “You have nothing until you have something”, “diplomacy is like untying knots on a fishing line for his son”, and “you play the ball from where it lands”.

There were also many happy admissions of historical ignorance. Since taking on the Ukraine brief a year ago, Kushner said, he had to learn “the algorithm of Europe and how complicated that is”, and he had to get abreast of “the local issues with Ukraine”.

blocks.caption: Jared Kushner, left, stands with the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, centre, and the US special envoy, Steve Witkoff, as they speak to the press in Dublin. Photograph: Peter Morrison/AP

blocks.text: As a businessman he brought a special expertise, he claimed. “Look at what’s happening in the Middle East with sanctions, with Russia, with Iran. I think that you have to understand economics in order to understand geopolitics because the two go together very, very closely,” he said.
But the main revelation was how much he believes the Ukraine conflict is not a case of an aggressor and a victim – but is simply a series of misunderstandings and miscommunication.

Indeed, he treated Vladimir Putin as if he were a masterful corporate executive quite willing to close the deal if he were only given the right economic incentives – instead of a man ready to sacrifice hundreds of thousands of Russians to reclaim part of a historical empire.

In the process, Kushner revealed – often inadvertently – that he has largely bought into the Russian narrative of a string of postwar missteps by Europe and the US coming to a head in Nato’s expansion eastwards after 9/11.

That, in turn, has led him to adopt Moscow’s central demand to reshape the European security order to allow Russia, without opprobrium, to retain land it has gained by force. Shining through his answers was a naive bias towards the aggressor, presented as a mediator’s desire to understand both parties.

Praise veering on awe for the Russian leader flowed. “Putin – people can like what he has done, they can not like what he has done – [but] he is a grand master of politics. He is a historic figure,” he said. Any sense that Putin may have blundered escaped him.

As to the rights and wrongs of invading another country, Kushner was blasé. “After all, most lines in Europe have changed over time and they are decided through war or peace, or concessions. It’s not about fairness or who is right or wrong. It’s about ending the killing,” he said.

He understood too why Putin could not offer a ceasefire: “He has very little confidence that if he stops the war, that he [will] be able to get to a postwar settlement that leads to not having a future war.”
To stop the killing, the killing has to go on.
What is more, Kushner was struck by the Russian leader’s self-control. “So far Putin has shown restraint and he has agreed not to use nuclear weapons and he has reassured us that is his intention.”

blocks.caption: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin shake hands during a meeting in China. Photograph: Vyacheslav Prokofyev/Reuters

blocks.text: Kushner denied that his boss had put any pressure on Volodymyr Zelenskyy, defying his interviewer to provide evidence – at which point Döpfner recited a list of examples, including only last month when Trump suggested that Ukraine should get a new leader.

Trump was “a strong counter-puncher,” argued Kushner, implying that Zelenskyy had thrown the first punch in a conflict that began with a Russian invasion. Relations with Ukraine were cooperative, he said before pointedly saying Kyiv needed things from the US, without which “Ukraine will not be safe in the future”.

After noting that “the territorial issue is now a little bit of a deadlock,” his strategic insight was that if a future security architecture for Europe could be agreed, the land question in Donbas would eventually follow.
In essence, he proposed a revival of the Russia-Nato council, one of the bodies eviscerated by Putin’s war.

He also envisioned Ukraine inside the European Union with security guarantees akin to those offered by Nato’s article five. But it was impossible at this stage to give “more specificity” about these guarantees in the detailed way Ukraine sought, he admitted.
So far neither Moscow or Kyiv have bought this plan, let alone a wary Europe.

Kushner tried to be polite about Europe, insisting it had to be at the negotiating table, but he could not stop himself characterising European military assistance to Ukraine as a “proxy war” against Russia.

As an analysis of why the Ukraine war had not ended inside the 24 hours Donald Trump promised, Kushner showed an alarming belief that the answer lay in granting more concessions to Putin, believing that the misunderstandings and misperceptions would then evaporate.

articles.title: Eastern US recovers from storms that snarled Thanksgiving travel as flooding continues
articles.summary:
Heavy rains and high winds downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia

Skies are clearing along the US eastern seaboard, and power was being restored to…

blocks.text: Skies are clearing along the US eastern seaboard, and power was being restored to hundreds of thousands of customers, whose Thanksgiving plans were disrupted by heavy rains and high winds that swept over the region Thursday.

The storms snarled travel, downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia. At its peak, nearly a million customers were without power and widespread coastal flooding was reported by Poweroutage.us.
“The bulk of the storm impacts are behind us, but tidal flooding will continue today,” the National Weather Service said early Friday.

The storms prompted the first-ever postponement of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade in New York City, and more than 2,200 flights to or from US destinations were delayed and more than 400 were cancelled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware.
On Friday, the service said total delays within, into, or out of the US stood at 485 and cancellations at 113.

In New Jersey widespread flooding even reached levels not seen since 2012, after Hurricane Sandy, and a state of emergency was put in place. The strongest wind gust reported was 82 mph in Mantoloking in Ocean county, the National Weather Service said.

The midwest and the south saw unusual snowfalls for the time of year, with St Louis, Missouri, getting 7.3in, and snow reported in Alabama and Tennessee. An ice arena in Wentzville, Missouri, was empty when the roof caved in at about 3am, according to the city
The storms are now giving way to winds and falling temperatures.

“The south and south-east US will start with very cold morning temperatures today and Saturday as lows drop into the upper 20s and the middle 30s,” the National Weather Service said. “Freeze headlines are in effect for portions of the deep south. High temperatures Saturday will begin to moderate into the 60s.”
In New York City, people were rescued from their cars amid flooding, said Zohran Mamdani, and similar rescues were reported in other coastal communities.
“There is no destination worth your safety,” the New York City mayor said.

Strong winds and flooding disrupted train lines, toppled trees and caused power outages on Thanksgiving night, New York City emergency management officials said. Several scaffolding structures collapsed in the wind, but no injuries were reported.

blocks.caption: People walk through a wet midtown Manhattan. Macy’s postponed its Thanksgiving Day parade to Saturday due to weather.   Photograph: Spencer Platt/Getty Images

blocks.text: The storms also flooded areas from North Carolina through to New Jersey as high tide rolled in. Roads were closed, and emergency workers were rescuing people from cars stranded in water.
Avalon, New Jersey, was seeing some of the worst flooding in its history, said Scott J Wahl, the borough’s business administrator.
Flood waters washed debris over the road, and a few drivers were rescued after driving around barricades into the waters, but no injuries were reported, Wahl said.
Lance Miller, 54, said flood waters in his Ocean City, New Jersey, neighbourhood were about a foot deep and that driving to the nearest supermarket would probably “destroy your car”.
The Margate City fire department near Atlantic City, New Jersey posted video on Facebook of water pouring through the city’s streets, even before heavy rains started.
A firefighter said the tide was coming in ferociously, even with an hour to go before its peak. Water closed in on houses, and sandbags were piled in front of businesses.

Some highways and bridges were temporarily closed. The nearly 18-mile (29-km) Chesapeake Bay bridge-tunnel in southern Virginia was closed for several hours on Thursday morning because of high winds, while NC 12, the only highway connecting Hatteras Island on the North Carolina Outer Banks to the mainland, was closed after seawater breached the dunes and covered the two-lane highway.

blocks.caption: The Lincoln Memorial during a rain storm in Washington DC. Photograph: Anna Rose Layden/Reuters

blocks.text: In Maryland, nearly 2 million water customers in Montgomery and Prince George’s counties were asked to conserve water because of intermittent power disruptions associated with the storm. Baltimore police closed several streets on Thursday night after storm surge caused flooding in waterfront neighborhoods.
The storms also prompted several brief tornado warnings on Thursday, including a rare twister south-east of Seattle, Washington.

Donald Trump signed a disaster declaration on Thursday for Florida in response to earlier flooding that damaged hundreds of homes and required water rescues. The US president had approved funding earlier this week, but gathered local officials on Thanksgiving to talk about it in a small signing ceremony at his home in West Palm Beach.
Meanwhile, high-tide driven waves and strong winds caused flooding along the Pacific coast on Thursday.
Record tides along the California coast forced evacuations in areas from Humboldt county in the far north to Ventura county near Los Angeles.
King tides were surging along the west coast.
Video showed a big wave tearing down part of the Pacifica pier in California on Wednesday, sending it into the ocean. Officials had closed the L-shaped pier in the summer after finding cracks.

articles.title: Kanal-Centre Pompidou, Brussels' most anticipated new art museum, opens its doors
articles.summary: A major addition to Europe's cultural scene: Kanal-Centre Pompidou, the new contemporary art museum in a former Citroen factory complex, celebrates its opening with a free, nonstop weekend program.

image.caption: The Kanal-Centre Pompidou was designed to occupy the former Citroen garage and factory complexImage: Koen Van Damme

blocks.text: Brussels is best known as the de facto capital of the European Union. But beyond its role as a political hub, it also boasts a thriving contemporary art scene.

Yet until now, the Belgian city didn't have a major museum of modern and contemporary art on the scale of Paris' Pompidou or London's Tate Modern. But this will now change with the opening of Kanal-Centre Pompidou on November 28.

The museum aims to "make Brussels a world-class cultural destination," on par with the Guggenheim in Bilbao or the MoMA in New York, Boris Dillies, the head of the regional government, told press agency AFP.
Behind this new museum is an ambitious architectural project involving the transformation of a vast industrial landmark into a multidisciplinary cultural institution.
A modern art museum inside a car factory
Instead of building the new museum from scratch, Kanal was designed to occupy the former Citroen garage and factory complex, built in 1933-34 beside the Brussels canal.

Originally standing as a symbol of modernity and industrial progress, the factory was a space where cars were serviced and assembled, as well as displayed. The former showroom has been transformed into as a glass-and-steel space that rises 21 meters (some 70 feet) high.

blocks.caption: The museum occupies a former Citroën factory complexImage: Bart Grietens

blocks.text: Rather than erasing the building's industrial past, the project's architects — noAarchitecten, EM2N and Sergison Bates, working together as Atelier Kanal — decided to celebrate its original structures. Vast concrete volumes and industrial details remain visible, creating a dialogue between the site's history and its new cultural purpose.
Like London's Tate Modern, which transformed a power station into a museum, Kanal shows how industrial architecture can gain a second life without losing its identity.

"Kanal reveals how architecture can reinvent the museum typology, not only as a place for art, but as a stage for the city and its citizens," Atelier Kanal said in a statement, adding that their concept for the former Citroen factory ensured that the space would be "renewed without being erased, made precise without being overdetermined and open to continued transformation."
Covering around 40,000 square meters (430,550 square feet), the complex is one of the largest cultural buildings in Belgium.
Kanal, Pompidou launch 5-year partnership

Kanal has established a partnership agreement with the Centre Pompidou in Paris that has guided both the international outlook of the new museum, as well as its intention to remain rooted in Brussels' local culture.
"A place for all people" was the founding vision of the Centre Pompidou, articulated by its architects Richard Rogers and Renzo Piano as they designed the iconic institution in the 1970s.

blocks.caption: 'A place for the people': The museum's cultural program includes activities for children Image: Koen Broos, 2025

blocks.text: Kanal's collaboration with the Centre Pompidou, which runs until 2031, gives the Brussels museum access to one of the world's greatest collections of modern and contemporary art. Visitors will be able to see works that normally reside in Paris, while also encountering pieces from Belgian collections and newly commissioned projects.

The Brussels museum has already announced some of the upcoming exhibitions that will be drawing from the Pompidou's collection during their five-year partnership: two photography exhibitions focusing on Robert Frank and Brassaï, as well as art exhibitions focusing on iconic figures of modernism: Robert and Sonia Delaunay, Georges Braque, Pablo Picasso and Henri Matisse.
The new institution, however, emphasizes that it's not a branch of the Pompidou. The partnership is rather envisioned as a dialogue between two museums with different perspectives and histories.
The Centre Pompidou itself has been closed for major renovations since September 2025, and is scheduled to reopen in 2030.
10 opening exhibitions

The headline exhibition, "A truly immense journey," brings together more than 350 works from the collections of Centre Pompidou, Kanal and numerous Belgian lenders, and will feature modern icons including Lygia Clark, Sonia Delaunay, Alberto Giacometti, Natalia Goncharova, Wifredo Lam and Henri Matisse.
Along with this show, nine other exhibitions fill the building.

One of them, "An infinite woman," focuses on how mass-produced image of a Mangbetu woman long served as a colonial symbol and how artists of African descent have reappropriated and subverted this imagery.

Another one, "Right to the City — Right to the Future," explores the architectural transformation of the Brussels' Quartier Nord, which was historically a working-class neighborhood that was largely cleared in the 1960s to become a high-rise business district — displacing over 15,000 residents.
Museum as a third space
Alongside modern and contemporary art, Kanal is dedicated to architecture, landscape and the performing arts.

This reflects a broader shift in the role of museums, which are increasingly expected to be places where people gather, exchange ideas and engage with contemporary issues rather than simply admire objects behind glass.

blocks.caption: The opening weekend will also feature DJs and concertsImage: Sofie de Backere

blocks.text: The opening program alone demonstrates the museum's ambitions, offering a 36-hour nonstop program of live performances, opening rituals, concerts, DJ sets, films, installations and workshops for children and families, with events open to everyone.

The exhibitions can also be visited for free during the inaugural weekend. Visitors, however, need to have previously booked a time slot; all 30,000 tickets were snapped up within 24 hours of their release.

articles.title: Quimbo: 3-in-1 coffee may be taxed if sugar content remains high
articles.summary: House Committee on Ways and Means Chairperson Miro Quimbo on Friday warned that 3-in-1 coffee could be subjected to taxation in three years if manufacturers fail to reduce the sugar content of their…

blocks.text: Published November 28, 2026 12:13am

House Committee on Ways and Means Chairperson Miro Quimbo on Friday warned that 3-in-1 coffee could be subjected to taxation in three years if manufacturers fail to reduce the sugar content of their products.
Unlike regular coffee, 3-in-1 coffee contains sugar and other caloric ingredients, making it a potential candidate for inclusion in the sweetened beverage tax, he explained in an online interview.
Quimbo said 3-in-1 coffee was exempted from the sweetened beverage tax when it was first implemented several years ago because it was widely consumed by ordinary Filipinos.
However, he noted that manufacturers have since increased the sugar content of their products.
Some members of the House of Representatives have proposed imposing a tax on 3-in-1 coffee, Quimbo said.
However, he said his committee was not inclined to support the proposal, citing the product's widespread consumption among lower-income Filipinos.
Still, Quimbo stressed the need to consider the health effects of excessive sugar consumption.

"Hindi kami puwedeng walang gawin pagdating diyan dahil kailangan natin kumbinsihin ang mga manufacturers na babaan o bawasan nila yung tamis nito. Kasi nagiging cause din ito ng diabetes na siyang nagiging pangunahing cause ng death na noncommunicable diseases sa ating bansa," Quimbo said.

(We cannot simply do nothing about this because we need to convince manufacturers to reduce the sweetness or sugar content of their products. This can also contribute to diabetes, which is one of the leading causes of death from noncommunicable diseases in our country.)
He said manufacturers could be given a three-year transition period to reformulate their products and lower their sugar content.
Otherwise, 3-in-1 coffee products exceeding a measurable sugar threshold could be subjected to taxation after the transition period, he added.
"But today, we are not going to tax it," Quimbo said.

In a statement, Presidential Legislative Liaison Office Secretary Joey Salceda said proposals to extend the sweetened beverage tax to sweetened coffee, including 3-in-1 mixes, should be evaluated on their own merits and not based on declining alcohol tax revenues.
"Sin taxes are punitive by design. They are meant to discourage socially undesirable behavior, not to compensate for declining revenues from other sin taxes," he said. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Canada’s top court upholds Quebec law barring public sector workers from wearing religious symbols
articles.summary:
Closely watched decision exposes tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights

Canada’s top court has largely upheld a

blocks.text: Canada’s top court has largely upheld a controversial secularism law in the province of Quebec barring public sector workers from wearing conspicuous religious symbols, in a closely watched decision that exposes the tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights.
In a 6-1 ruling released on Friday morning, the supreme court found Quebec was permitted to shield the law, Bill 21, from most court challenges on the grounds that it violated charter rights.
“Bill 21 is rooted in Quebec’s legitimate and historical commitment to ensuring the laicity of the state in a free and democratic society,” chief justice Richard Wagner wrote in the majority opinion.

Canada’s top court says the four days of hearings from earlier in the year marked one of the longest in its 151-year history. Fifty-one interveners participated, including six attorneys general – also a record number. The court’s website crashed on Friday morning when the judgment was released.
While the judgment was celebrated by some in Quebec who considered it a vindication of the province’s fight, it was swiftly criticised by religious civil liberties groups.

“We cannot exist in a country as free people, where governments can literally go to the electorate and say, ‘I’m gonna take away the rights of a certain group of minorities’, because it’s popular and to play wedge politics with the charter rights of Canadians,” Stephen Brown, chief executive of the National Council of Canadian Muslims, told reporters at a press conference. “If that is the case, we don’t have a charter of rights and freedoms. We have a charter of suggestions and permissions.”

Passed in 2019, Quebec’s secularism law, Bill 21, bars workers including lawyers, judges, police and teachers from wearing religious symbols such as a hijab, turban, kippah or a cross while on the job.

Central to the case – and the reason provincial governments across the country are closely watching the result – is the “notwithstanding clause”, a constitutional mechanism that allows elected governments to override certain fundamental rights and freedoms guaranteed by Canada’s Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

The clause is the result of political compromise from the 1980s, when the federal government set out to replace the existing British North America Act with a new constitution. Provinces feared that under a new constitution, courts would become too powerful, undermining the authority of the elected government. A compromise was hashed out: in cases when a government – provincial or federal – felt that the courts had overstepped, they could invoke the clause to override certain charter rights of citizens.

Some fundamental rights, including protections of religious freedom, equality and speech, could be suspended. But voting, as well as language rights, were untouchable, ensuring Canadians could remove a government if they wanted. A government could only invoke the clause for five years. Before they could renew it, they would first have to face voters.

In its decision, the supreme court rejected most arguments that Bill 21 violated portions of the charter that are not subject to the notwithstanding clause, including guarantees relating to the equality of men and women and the education rights of Quebec’s English-speaking minority.

Quebec’s use of the clause with Bill 21 was notable – and controversial – in that it was the first time the notwithstanding clause had been invoked pre-emptively in an attempt to shield the law from court challenges. Quebec also passed Bill 96, which sought to strengthen French language protections – again pre-emptively invoking the notwithstanding clause.

But groups affected by those laws can still challenge them and many teachers, religious and civil liberties groups argued it was a clear violation of constitutional rights and reflected government overreach. Quebec’s government has defended the law, saying it is constitutionally valid.

In April 2021, a Quebec superior court judge described the effects of the law as “cruel”, saying it “dehumanises” the people it targets, but conceded the statute could not be struck down because it was protected by the notwithstanding clause. Quebec’s court of appeal also upheld the law in February 2024 on the same grounds.

In its 520-page judgment, the court did find that element of the law infringed on democratic rights protected by the charter, including preventing elected members of Quebec’s National Assembly who wear face coverings for religious reasons from participating in the legislative process.

In a 4-3 decision, the court also endorsed the ability of lower courts to issue “judicial declarations” on laws protected by the notwithstanding clause, giving judges the power to declare a law in violation of the charter, even though the law would be permitted to stand.
The court’s decision was celebrated in Quebec, where the governing Parti Québécois has looked for wedges with the federal government and institutions like the supreme court.
The premier, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, had previously said his province’s right to decide its own laws was at risk.

Canada only recently fended off a threat to national unity after voters in Alberta rejected the initial stages of a separatist push. But Quebec’s newly elected government has shown an eagerness to clash with the prime minister, Mark Carney.

The supreme court’s judgment comes on the same day an appeal will be heard regarding a superior court decision that forces Quebec’s members of the national assembly to swear allegiance to King Charles to sit in the Salon Bleu – the chamber of the assembly. Lawmakers from a number of parties in the province recently refused to swear the oath of allegiance.

articles.title: Serbia's Student List runs chemistry professor Radomir Saicic for president
articles.summary: After ousting strongman Aleksandar Vucic, Serbia's student movement has now nominated academic Radomir Saicic for the upcoming presidential vote. Saicic accused the "outgoing regime" of trying to…

image.caption: Saicic has publicly supported the protest movement and took part in their rallies against strongman Aleksandar VucicImage: Maxim Konankov/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: A long-time supporter of the Serbian student movement, chemistry professor and researcher Radomir Saicic, is set to run for president on behalf of the Student List in late December.
Saicic accepted the nomination on Friday, a day after Serbia's new parliament scheduled the ballot for December 27.
We were there when Serbia's student movement toppled the government
In his acceptance speech, the Belgrade University lecturer said state institutions, including its president, needed to "win back public trust."
"It's time to restore dignity to the office of Serbian president," he said.

"Once we can agree with each other about things that matter to all of us despite our differences, Serbia will have the strength to decide its future on its own, and to have its voice heard and respected in the world," he added.
Vucic barred from running again

The 65-year-old is one of the lawmakers in the new assembly, which was formed in the wake of the Student List ousting the regime of Serbia's longtime strongman ruler Aleksandar Vucic at the parliamentary polls last month.
Lessons from Serbia: How students defeated an authoritarian leader
Vucic is banned by the constitution from running for president after winning two terms. He has hinted at his party boycotting the presidential vote.

While the office of the Serbian president is officially far less powerful that the office of Serbian prime minister, Vucic managed to organize his rule around himself during his time as prime minister and then hold on to levers of power while serving as president.
Saicic sees Kosovo as 'occupied territory'
On Friday, Saicic accused the "outgoing regime" of "still trying to collapse our state."
"This past decade was marred by the breakdown of the rule of law, corruption, and hate speech," he said.
Saicic, a member of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Art, is seen by many as a moderate nationalist and a traditionalist.

He has notably described the neigboring, Albanian-dominated Kosovo, as "temporarily occupied territory," keeping in line with Belgrade's long-running policy of treating Kosovo as a breakaway province.
The scandals that rocked Serbia and are shaping the election
The presidential candidate has also urged a "productive relationship" with Russia, pointing to Serbia's energy needs.
Saicic pledges humility with Bible quote

While seemingly reticent on the topic of the European Union, Saicic told reporters on Friday that he has a "fundamentally positive stance toward Europe and European values," pointing to examples including environment protection, academic education, the rule of law, science and technological progress.
"All of these things we should develop as much as possible, not for the sake of meeting some formal criteria, but to actually be what we are supposed to be," he said.
Saicic has sought to present himself as a devout Orthodox Christian while simultaneously criticizing the Serbian church leaders for aligning with the Vucic regime.
In his Friday speech, Saicic quoted the Bible, saying that "whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant."

articles.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader convicted over further 123 deaths
articles.summary: Paul Mackenzie is found guilty of killing followers, weeks after being jailed for the mass murder of children.

blocks.text: A court in Kenya has convicted the leader of a doomsday Christian cult of the manslaughter of 123 of his followers.
Paul Mackenzie was found guilty in Mombasa of ordering his followers, all adults, to fast to death in Shakahola forest near the coast between January 2021 and September 2023.
Earlier this month Mackenzie was jailed for 200 years for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children, in the same mass killing.
Mackenzie had pleaded not guilty to manslaughter and one of his lawyers said he would appeal against the conviction after sentencing, Reuters news agency reports.
The court also convicted 29 others including Mackenzie's wife, Rhoda Mumbua Maweu, of their part in the manslaughter.
Sixty defendants were acquitted. The Director of Public Prosecutions indicated that an appeal would be launched against their acquittal.
The self-styled pastor was arrested in 2023 after the discovery of more than 400 bodies in shallow graves.

The court found Mackenzie had "systematically persuaded his followers to fast until they died", Kenya's Office of The Director of Public Prosecutions said in a statement on Friday's verdict, which it described as "the final conviction" in the Shakahola cases against him.
"Children were to go first, then women and then men, with Mackenzie himself meant to die last," the office said.
The prosecution argued that Mackenzie and his accomplices had acted together as part of a suicide pact to fast to death in order to "meet Jesus".
Witnesses testified that he had preached that education, medicine and ornaments were sinful.
Those who opposed his teachings were beaten to death, according to the verdict in his trial for the murder of 191 people.
The defendants claimed that the victims had fasted out of their own free will.
The Shakahola deaths have shone a spotlight on the lack of oversight of rogue religious activities and how they could have carried on for so long.
The gravity of the case prompted President William Ruto to set up a commission of inquiry, although this was later declared unconstitutional.

articles.title: Internal probe led to graft case vs employees – Landbank
articles.summary: The Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP) said its internal investigation prompted the filing of a graft complaint against three long-sacked employees and a businessman over alleged irregularities…

blocks.text: November 28, 2026 | 12:00am
Land Bank of the Philippines
Businessworld / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP) said its internal investigation prompted the filing of a graft complaint against three long-sacked employees and a businessman over alleged irregularities involving a P115-million loan.

In a statement, the state-run firm said it filed the complaint before the Office of the Ombudsman on May 26, 2022 after uncovering alleged irregularities in a loan transaction granted to American Boulevard Trading Corp. (ABTC).
“The ombudsman’s decision to pursue graft charges is a result of the complaint filed by Landbank and validates the bank’s actions in bringing the matter before the proper authorities,” it said.

The ombudsman previously announced that it found prima facie evidence with reasonable certainty of conviction against former LBP first vice president Lolita Silva, former assistant vice president Danilo Dayanghirang, former account officer Ronaldo Robles and ABTC president and chairman Alberto Ching for violation of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act.
Landbank said the transaction was processed by the three former employees, identified as Silva, Dayanghirang and Robles, who had already left the state-run lender in January and March 2020.
Silva’s employment ended on Jan. 31, 2020, while Dayanghirang and Robles left the bank on March 3, 2020 and Jan. 17, 2020, respectively.
The bank said it maintains zero tolerance for misconduct and would take appropriate action against officials or employees found accountable.
Landbank net income had risen by eight percent to P37.53 billion as of end-September from P34.86 billion last year.

articles.title: Sandiganbayan affirms grant of bail to Revilla
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan Third Division has upheld its granting of bail to former senator Ramon Revilla Jr. in his malversation case involving an alleged ghost flood control project in Pandi, Bulacan.

blocks.text: November 28, 2026 | 12:00am
Sandiganbayan
Philstar.com / Irra Lising

MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Third Division has upheld its granting of bail to former senator Ramon Revilla Jr. in his malversation case involving an alleged ghost flood control project in Pandi, Bulacan.
In a 49-page resolution, the anti-graft court denied the prosecution’s motion for reconsideration that sought to overturn the grant of bail to Revilla while the case is undergoing trial.

The court also denied the motions of former public works officials Brice Hernandez, Arjay Domasig, Jaypee Mendoza, Juanito Mendoza, Emelita Juat and Christina Pineda to reconsider the denial of their bail petitions.

The anti-graft court maintained that the funds involved in the case are not public in nature as far as Revilla is concerned. It said the boxes of cash allegedly received by him supposedly came from a pool of funds coming from contributions of private contractors.

It said that even if it were to be assumed that the prosecution had managed to present strong evidence of guilt that the former senator may have received cash from private contractors, it would only prove the existence of bribery, which is a bailable offense, and not malversation due to the private nature of the funds.

The Sandiganbayan also said the prosecution was not able to prove that there was conspiracy on the part of Revilla as it alleged that Revilla facilitated the funding for the project when it was included in the national budget.
It ruled that Revilla’s participation in the legislative process was diluted and attenuated.
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla had slammed the original grant of bail, saying the issue appeared to have been “natrabaho.”
There was no comment from the two associate justices who approved the bail – Ronald Moreno and Fritz Bryn Anthony delos Santos. Third Division chairman Karl Miranda had voted to deny the bail.

articles.title: Public officials told: No Christmas solicitations
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman has warned public officials and employees against soliciting donations for Christmas parties and other unauthorized purposes, after suspending a barangay secretary in…

blocks.text: November 28, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Ombudsman has warned public officials and employees against soliciting donations for Christmas parties and other unauthorized purposes, after suspending a barangay secretary in Makati over solicitation letters using official government letterhead.
Olegario was found to have issued letters in December 2025 asking for cash or in-kind donations from private individuals for the barangay officials’ and personnel’s Christmas party.

The ombudsman said that using the authority and resources of public office resources to solicit donations “for a purpose not shown to be a governmental function is inconsistent with the standards of integrity and propriety expected of public employees.”

“It creates the appearance that the government itself is requesting private individuals to provide money or property for the benefit of its personnel. This is precisely the type of conduct that may diminish public confidence,” it said.

articles.title: Group pushes back on coffee tax
articles.summary: A local coffee group has called out a proposal to impose excise taxes on coffee, warning that this could undermine the development of the country’s coffee industry.

blocks.text: November 28, 2026 | 12:00am
A steaming cup of coffee on a bed of coffee beans.
Márcio Carvalho via Pexels
MANILA, Philippines — A local coffee group has called out a proposal to impose excise taxes on coffee, warning that this could undermine the development of the country’s coffee industry.

In a statement, the Philippine Coffee Guild warned that any new tax on coffee could lead to higher retail prices, squeeze the margins of small roasters and affect the prices buyers can offer farmers for their harvests.
“It could show up in the price of a cup, in what a small roaster can afford to absorb or in what a buyer can offer a farmer for a harvest,” the group said.

The statement was issued after a representative of the Distilled Spirits Association of the Philippines suggested imposing excise taxes on coffee products, as alcohol consumption declines amid changing consumer preferences.

The coffee guild urged Congress and the Department of Finance to retain existing excise tax exemptions for coffee and to consult farmers, cooperatives, small businesses and other industry stakeholders before considering any new tax measure affecting the sector.
“Tax policy should support the people who grow it and keep it accessible to the people who drink it,” the Coffee Guild said.
The group also noted that coffee businesses already pay applicable income taxes, value-added tax or percentage tax and customs duties.
The group said alcohol and coffee should not be treated the same way under tax policies, noting that excise taxes are meant to curb consumption of products linked to adverse health outcomes.

articles.title: President Marcos to non-commissioned AFP officers: We stand behind you
articles.summary: President Marcos has asked non-commissioned officers (NCOs) of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) to keep up the good work as he assured them of the government’s full support in the…

blocks.text: November 28, 2026 | 12:00am
“As your commander-in-chief, I want you to know that just as you stand in defense of our nation, we will always stand behind you,” Marcos said on Facebook.
Bongbong Marcos / Facebook Page

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos has asked non-commissioned officers (NCOs) of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) to keep up the good work as he assured them of the government’s full support in the performance of their duties.

Marcos joined the members of the AFP Council of Sergeants Major in a boodle fight at the General Headquarters Building in Camp General Emilio Aguinaldo, Quezon City, in celebration of the council’s 57th anniversary on Thursday.?
“So we, on our part, will provide all the support we can and indeed, we are well aware of the great importance of your work, of what you are doing,” Marcos said.?
The President recognized the invaluable contributions of NCOs in ensuring the operational effectiveness and continuity of leadership within the military establishment.
“The officers command the AFP. But the NCOs are the backbone of the military,” he added.?
He noted that the NCOs are responsible for translating orders into action and ensuring the successful execution of military operations.?
Marcos underscored their vital role in bridging the gap between commissioned officers and enlisted men and women, particularly younger military personnel.?
He acknowledged their responsibilities in preserving institutional memory and military traditions, recognizing outstanding personnel and assisting those experiencing difficulties.?
Marcos encouraged the NCOs to communicate openly with their superiors regarding the problems, concerns and needs of their troops.?
“When you see something that needs to be done or you see a problem or you hear something about the needs of our troops, please tell us all,” Marcos added.?
He said that every officer in the chain of command, must be informed about the conditions and welfare of military personnel.?

articles.title: Impeachment court summons BOC official, Carpio business partner
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court has subpoenaed a Bureau of Customs (BOC) official and a former co-owner of Cale88 Foods Corp. to testify on the company’s business operations and export records…

blocks.text: November 28, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court has subpoenaed a Bureau of Customs (BOC) official and a former co-owner of Cale88 Foods Corp. to testify on the company’s business operations and export records when proceedings on the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte resume on Dec. 1.?
Impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol said subpoenas were issued on Nov. 25 and served on both witnesses on Nov. 26 ahead of the hearings from Dec. 1 to 4.

The witnesses are Customs Deputy Commissioner for assessment and operations coordinating group Agaton Teodoro Uvero and Dr. Lourdes Tingson-Lebosada, who is also the Vice President’s dentist.?Uvero is expected to testify on Cale88 Foods’ exportation records held by the BOC and identify documents concerning the company’s registration and shipments.

On the other hand, Lebosada, who previously co-owned Cale88 with Duterte’s husband Manases Carpio, was directed to testify on the company’s organizational structure, government registrations, business operations, finances, ownership and transactions.
Both witnesses were ordered to appear at 10 a.m. on the scheduled hearing dates and submit three certified true copies and electronic copies of the required records in three USB flash drives.?

Tongol said the respondent’s initial list of two witnesses satisfies the minimum requirement for the resumption of hearings on Dec. 1. Any additional witnesses for the Dec. 2 to 4 hearings must comply with an earlier order requiring five days’ advance notice and at least two witnesses for each hearing day.

The court will automatically reproduce documents submitted in compliance with the subpoenas and furnish copies to both the prosecution and defense panels, subject to restrictions on records covered by statutory confidentiality.
The impeachment court is set to resume proceedings on Dec. 1 at 10 a.m., while exhibit marking continues before the Clerk of Court.?Witness lineup
Meanwhile, the House prosecution panel wants the full lineup of the defense’s witness list after only two names have so far been identified.
House prosecutor and Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon hoped that the defense would provide a clearer picture of its remaining presentation.
“We will give them the chance to have that full witness list. However, there is none yet,” he said.
“Hopefully they can present new witnesses, particularly to fill in the missing details sought by senator-judges pertaining to Cale88,” the lawmaker added.
House lead prosecutor and Batangas 2nd district Rep. Gerville Luistro, for her part, urged the defense to just come clean.

“If there really are more witnesses, reveal them, and if there are none, be transparent to the impeachment court so that the impeachment court can strategize how to wrap up, how to conclude in a timely manner,” she said in a radio interview. — Daphne Galvez

articles.title: ERC orders P1.99 billion Meralco refund
articles.summary: The Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) has ordered Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) to return around P1.99 billion to its more than eight million customers over three months.

blocks.text: November 28, 2026 | 12:00am

The refund translates to an average rate of P0.1536 per kilowatt-hour (kWh) and will appear on customers’ bills as a separate line item labeled “RAB Refund,” the ERC said, following its commission meeting on Nov. 26.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — The Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) has ordered Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) to return around P1.99 billion to its more than eight million customers over three months.
Residential and small commercial customers, meanwhile, will receive a larger refund of P0.2611 per kWh or about P52 for typical households consuming 200 kWh a month.
Francis Saturnino Juan, ERC chairman and CEO, told The STAR yesterday the refund is expected to be credited to customers’ bills starting next month.

The refund stems from the ERC’s revaluing of Meralco’s regulatory asset base (RAB) and disallowing certain pension and employee benefit expenses, in compliance with a Supreme Court ruling arising from a petition filed by the National Association of Electricity Consumers for Reforms Inc.
The refund order comes as a timely relief for Meralco customers, who are grappling with high electricity rates amid rising fuel prices, a weaker peso and tight power supply conditions.
These factors have driven up generation charges, which cover the cost of electricity procured from suppliers and were the primary contributor to the increase in Meralco’s overall rate this month.

“By acting decisively and completing this case now, the commission ensures that the amount due to consumers is returned when they need it most and that the refund will help cushion the impact of these increases on their monthly bills,” Juan said.

Under its ruling, the Supreme Court directed the ERC to reassess the valuation of Meralco’s RAB and establish guidelines for determining whether expenses not directly and entirely related to its operations may be passed on to consumers, either wholly or partially.
While recognizing that pension costs are legitimate expenses, the court held that Meralco must substantiate the amounts it seeks to recover from consumers.

articles.title: Pump prices seen going down by P3 per liter
articles.summary: Gasoline and diesel prices could be headed for another rollback next week, with industry projections of P3 to P3.50 per liter decrease for both following four days of trading in the Mean of Platts…

blocks.text: November 28, 2026 | 12:00am
Oil prices remained relatively low this week amid expectations of a supply surplus following increased crude loadings from Middle Eastern terminals outside the strategic Strait of Hormuz.
The STAR / Michael Varcas, file

MANILA, Philippines — Gasoline and diesel prices could be headed for another rollback next week, with industry projections of P3 to P3.50 per liter decrease for both following four days of trading in the Mean of Platts Singapore.

Jetti Petroleum president Leo Bellas said the development overshadowed concerns over shipping risks as attacks in the narrow waterway, which typically handles about 20 percent of global oil and gas supplies, continued.
“Product prices also eased further this week, as strong supply outlook amid rising Chinese exports continues to loosen tight availability of both gasoline and diesel in the region,” Bellas said.
He, however, warned that continued attacks on shipping vessels in the Strait of Hormuz could have an immediate impact on oil supplies from the Middle East.
With one trading day remaining, the projected price reductions may still increase or decrease. If implemented, next week’s rollback would mark the fourth straight week of cuts.
The Department of Energy is expected to announce the prescribed price adjustments on Monday that will take effect the following day.

Meanwhile, state-run Philippine National Oil Co. (PNOC) continues to advance the establishment of the government-maintained strategic petroleum reserve (SPR), which President Marcos described as a national priority.

“For the Philippines, our priority is clear: we are advancing our (SPR), backed by the robust infrastructure and financing required to sustain it,” Marcos said during the 4th Asia Zero-Emission Community Leaders’ Meeting in Manila.
The SPR, which will be located at the PNOC Industrial Park in Mariveles, Bataan, targets a total storage capacity of 15 million barrels of diesel, enough to cover about 75 days of demand.
The project’s initial phase involves the construction of six large storage tanks with a combined capacity of one million barrels. The first tank is targeted for completion by the end of 2027.
The remaining 14 million barrels of storage capacity, meanwhile, will be built through public-private partnerships and consortium arrangements.

articles.title: Dutch authorities seize 26 critically endangered turtles from luggage of passenger bound for Hong Kong
articles.summary: The tiny Vallarta mud turtle was only discovered in 2018. It's critically endangered with around 300 thought to live in the wild. Almost one tenth of that number were stashed in a traveler's luggage,…

image.caption: Authorities in the Netherlands seized 26 of the critically endangered critters on November 21; that's equivalent to almost one-tenth of the entire population estimated to be at large in the wildImage: NVWA

blocks.text: The Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA) said on Friday that it had seized more than two dozen critically endangered turtles that customs officers found in a passenger's luggage at Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport.

The Vallarta mud turtles discovered in the luggage of a man flying to Hong Kong via Schiphol are endemic to Mexico. They were only formally discovered and catalogued in 2018 and are one of the smallest of all known genuses of turtle.
"These highly rare and protected turtles were presumably taken from the wild in Mexico, where an estimated population of only about 300 of these animals remain," the NVWA said in a press release.
How were the turtles discovered and smuggled?

Dutch customs agents discovered the animals on November 21 during a regular inspection and then alerted the NVWA, as the responsible agency for such cases, on realizing that they had uncovered live fauna.
Police then arrested the man at the NVWA's request, and the NVWA said in Friday's statement that he was still in custody, with federal prosecutors continuing their investigations.

"Most of the turtles were packed in a box alongside a toy car, while others were placed inside a sealed sock within a suitcase," the NVWA wrote. "The animals had been wrapped in duct tape, which prevented them from moving. All of the turtles survived the journey."
Authorities said the turtles were being housed at a specialized rescue facility, "where the duct tape was carefully removed," and where they were "receiving the care they require."
What are Vallarta mud turtles?
Vallarta mud turtles are exceptionally small freshwater turtles that only entered the taxonomical record in 2018, endemic to a very small area in western Mexico.
Relatively little is known about the creature owing both to its recent discovery and the damage to its habitat caused by urbanization and a growing tourist trade in the Mexican state of Jalisco.

The Turtle Island organization in Graz, Austria — which recently started breeding the turtles in Austria as a "genetic reservoir for eventual rewilding" and is working to help preserve them in Mexico — considers it "the world's smallest turtle species," and estimates that "over 99%" of its natural habitat has been lost to urbanization.
Roads and traffic are a particular risk for the slow-moving creatures.

"Despite strict protections, their small size and striking appearance make them prime targets for illegal collectors," Turtle Island says when detailing other risks to the tiny animals, that are not known to grow larger than 10 centimeters (less than 4 inches) in length.

The IUCN Red List classifies it as "Critically Endangered" and it is subject to the highest level of protection under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES).

"The suspected poaching of 26 of these turtles from the wild may have reduced the population by nearly 10%," the NVWA wrote, basing its figure on the estimated population of around 300 of the turtles in the wild.

The agency urged people to report any suspected instances of illegal trade of protected animal or plant species, whether "via online forums, marketplaces, bird fairs, or antique and curiosity markets."

articles.title: DICT: No money stolen from accounts in reported government data breaches
articles.summary: No money was stolen from accounts in connection with reported data breaches involving several government agencies, based on the information currently available to the Department of Information and…

blocks.text: Published November 27, 2026 11:46pm

No money was stolen from accounts in connection with reported data breaches involving several government agencies, based on the information currently available to the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), Secretary Robert Joseph De Claro said.

“What I know is that in terms of critical breaches, wala namang nanakaw sa mga accounts in terms of monetary. So the breaches are information that are typically already out there,” he said in an interview on the sidelines of the 2026 ROK-Philippines-ASEAN AI+ Connectivity Forum in Makati City on Thursday.
(What I know is that, in terms of critical breaches, no money was stolen from the accounts. So the breaches are information that are typically already out there.)
The DICT is continuing to examine and investigate the reported data breach at the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR).

De Claro said that the DICT monitors government agencies for possible cybersecurity breaches. Once a breach is detected, the agency concerned is immediately notified and required to submit a report within two hours.

“In some cases, mas malawak yung investigation. So kaya siguro hindi pa nalalabas yung results. But I think in due time, malalabas na yung results with regards to ano ba yung data breach na nangyari,” De Claro said.

(In some cases, the investigations are more extensive, which may explain why the results have not yet been released. However, I believe the findings on what exactly happened in the data breach will be made public in due time.)
The DICT chief also acknowledged that cyber threats are becoming increasingly sophisticated, particularly with the use of artificial intelligence (AI).

In response, the DICT is working to strengthen the country's cybersecurity capabilities while pursuing broader regional cooperation with fellow ASEAN member states and countries with more advanced cybersecurity technologies.

“When you talk about cybersecurity, we really need to enhance our regional cooperation with our ASEAN brothers and also work with more advanced countries that protect and build cybersecurity solutions,” De Claro said. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Palace, several senators reject proposed coffee tax
articles.summary: Malacañang and several senators on Friday expressed opposition to a proposal to impose taxes on coffee products.
articles.byline: GISELLE OMBAY, TINA PANGANIBAN-PEREZ, GMA News

blocks.text: Malacañang and several senators on Friday expressed opposition to a proposal to impose taxes on coffee products.
In a statement, Presidential Legislative Liaison Office Secretary Joey Salceda said the government opposes taxing coffee itself.

"If more Filipinos are drinking coffee instead of alcohol, that is a good thing. It means that sin taxes on alcohol are working as designed. Simply put, you can drive after drinking coffee. You should not drive after drinking alcohol. The distinction is that simple," Salceda said.

During the Senate plenary deliberations on the proposed P378.629-billion budget of the Department of Health (DOH) and its attached agencies and corporations for 2027, Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian also opposed the proposal, noting that coffee is widely consumed in the Philippines.
He said that even workers who render overtime rely on coffee to stay awake.

"Personally, I don't think taxing coffee is a good idea. Well, first of all, coffee drinker po ang Pilipinas. Ang dami ngang Starbucks dito, ang daming mga coffee shops. Naging pastime natin 'yan," he said.
(Personally, I don't think taxing coffee is a good idea. First of all, the Philippines has many coffee drinkers. There are so many Starbucks and coffee shops. Drinking coffee has become our pastime.)
"We should also be sensitive to the products that our farmers, fishermen, and also our ordinary kababayans drink if they want to go overtime," he added.
Gatchalian also welcomed the commitment of House members not to pursue any proposal to tax coffee products.
The proposal to tax coffee in the Philippines was earlier raised by Olivia Limpe-Aw, president of the Distilled Spirits Association of the Philippines.
Senator Pia Cayetano, meanwhile, welcomed the statement of House ways and means committee chairperson Miro Quimbo that any proposal to impose taxes on coffee products was "dead for good."
"So hindi na 'yan makakarating sa 'tin kasi I'm one with you na 'yung product nga na 'yun, tinutulungan nga natin 'yung farmers," Cayetano said.
(So that will no longer reach the Senate because I share your view that the product actually helps our farmers.)
"On that note, buhay pa rin ang kape sa Pilipinas (the coffee industry in the Philippines is still alive). No tax, no tax on coffee!" she added.
Senator Joel Villanueva also weighed in on the proposal.
"'Pag 'yan ang pinag-usapan, Mr. President, maghahalo ang tinalupan sa binalatan (If that matter is discussed, Mr. President, all hell will break loose)," Villanueva said.
Tax on 3-in-1 coffee?
Meanwhile, Quimbo said 3-in-1 coffee could be subjected to taxation in the next few years if manufacturers fail to reduce the sugar content of their products.
Unlike regular coffee, 3-in-1 coffee contains sugar and other caloric ingredients, making it a potential candidate for inclusion in the sweetened beverage tax, he explained.
Quimbo said 3-in-1 coffee was exempted from the sweetened beverage tax when it was first implemented several years ago because it was widely consumed by ordinary Filipinos.
However, he noted that manufacturers have since increased the sugar content of their products.
Some members of the House of Representatives have proposed imposing a tax on 3-in-1 coffee, Quimbo said.
However, he said his committee was not inclined to support the proposal, citing the product's widespread consumption among lower-income Filipinos.
Still, Quimbo stressed the need to consider the health effects of excessive sugar consumption and encourage manufacturers to reduce the sugar content of their products.
He said manufacturers could be given a three-year transition period to reformulate their products and lower their sugar content.
Otherwise, 3-in-1 coffee products exceeding a measurable sugar threshold could be subjected to taxation after the transition period, he added.
Salceda said proposals to extend the sweetened beverage tax to sweetened coffee, including 3-in-1 mixes, should be evaluated on their own merits and not based on declining alcohol tax revenues.
"Sin taxes are punitive by design. They are meant to discourage socially undesirable behavior, not to compensate for declining revenues from other sin taxes," he said. —VBL, GMA News
